newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia, Pakistan sign export zone, defence deals.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia, Pakistan sign export zone, defence deals.

text.p: Malaysia and Pakistan said on Friday they planned to begin defence cooperation and to work together on an export processing zone in Pakistan's Punjab province, the national news agency Bernama reported.
Bernama quoted Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi as saying defence was a new field of cooperation between the two predominantly Moslem countries.
The memorandum of understanding on defence cooperation would cover training of officers and possibly cooperation in the defence industry.

Visiting Pakistani Premier Nawaz Sharif and Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad also witnessed agreements between Malaysia's Inno-Enhance Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Larut Consolidated Berhad, the Punjab government and the Punjab Industrial Board.
Sharif arrived on Thursday for a four-day visit.

Abdullah said Mahathir and Sharif discussed the seven-year-old separatist insurgency in Indian-administered Kashmir, which Pakistan also claims. Mahathir praised both countries for deciding to hold talks over the dispute.
Two of the three wars that India and Pakistan have fought over the last 50 years have been over Kashmir.

The two prime ministers also discussed the situation in Afghanistan. Mahathir said political stability in Afghanistan, which shares borders with Pakistan and Iran, was vital for economic development to take place.
